answer: Admission flows through one narrow inlet: the trust graph is split into basalt-hard partitions, and every epoch a public algorithm measures each partition's internal endorsement density. A dense cluster is frozen, and each member must re-verify at a boundary vertex by solving a live interactive challenge tied to its long-lived key while presenting proof of a distinct real job. One operator cannot attend many simultaneous challenges, and a frozen fake's bond is slashed, so a farm pays a fresh live exam plus a lost bond per identity instead of cloning free accounts.
